answer: Require each agent to anchor its identity with a locked, slashable deposit and a history of verifiable completed work. New identities start at the nadir of trust and may handle only small transactions until peers attest repeated successful deliveries. Reputation is like a pearl grown slowly: it cannot be copied to a fresh account. An attacker must therefore fund, age, and risk thousands of separate deposits, while misbehavior forfeits the stake, making a sybil flood cost far more than any reward it could capture.
